title: Concert structure and Bessie Smith as a person
summary: Bessie was only in the concert, liked to play tonk and drink, and Oxley's then-wife was a chorus girl on the show.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. Anything else about that show that you can think of while we're on that, if you can think of anything else about the whole company, the other acts or anything in the minstrel show too? Now, Bessie was never in the minstrel part of it though. She didn't sing anything in that. No, see. No.
See, on the, in the concert, well, they had a couple of acts, you know, that they would do, you know, to make the concert a little longer, you know.
Sort of like in between, while she'd rest, they'd put on something else. That's right.
See, and they'd bring her on maybe before the last act, you see. And after she'd come on, then the last act, and that was it, you see.
Now, the other thing, I mean, she used to like to play tonk, you know. Yeah.
Yeah, she used to like her chords, you know, that's one thing.
Now, my former wife was on that show with me when she died. She lives back on St. Philip Street.
Now, she remembers too, but she's right there.
That's right. Aunt Bessie was pretty good friend, you know. Yeah. And she was a chorus girl.

Did Bessie seem in pretty good health? I never did know Bessie Smith except to see her on the stage. Oh, yeah, she was a good one. She seemed in still good health. She was. When I last saw her, she looked good, you know. She was always pretty heavy, but it seemed... She was in pretty good health. Good health and spirits as far as I could tell. That's right. She wasn't really so old either. No. I think, you know, maybe around 40 or something. That's right.
She used to like her little juice, of course. We used to always get our little bottles together.
A lot of people did, yeah. Yeah.
